tasks.locator: Results > Total Psychopathological Symptoms > Single-Day vs Multiple-Day Studies; Table, 'Placebo condition' and 'Length of ketamine infusion before symptom assessment' columns; Discussion > Strengths and Limitations, 4th paragraph
tasks.extracted: The dummy condition was saline in 35 of the 36 healthy-volunteer studies and not reported in one. Two studies gave ketamine and placebo on the same day and 17 on different days, and the same-day design gave a larger pooled total-symptom effect (2.29, 95% CI 1.69 to 2.89, against 1.39, 1.12 to 1.66; P = .007 for the difference), which the authors explain either by unblinding or by better control of day-to-day variation; for positive and negative symptoms the two designs did not differ. The rating time was reported for 17 of the 36 studies and fell between 1 and 120 minutes after the infusion began. In the same Strengths and Limitations paragraph the authors state that further work is needed to characterise the dose-response relationship and the time course of these effects, so the review itself fixes no recovery time.

tasks.locator: Discussion > Ketamine Model of Schizophrenia, only paragraph; Results > Total Psychopathological Symptoms, Positive Psychotic Symptoms and Negative Symptoms > Blinding Method subsections
tasks.extracted: The authors qualify their own positive-versus-negative comparison: the negative-symptom analysis included an extra study that used a continuous infusion alone, which they say may have reduced that effect, while the positive-symptom analysis included more unblinded studies and fewer studies giving both conditions on the same day; they conclude that the association is larger for positive symptoms while calling the negative-symptom effect large as well. Blinding status did not change the pooled effect significantly in any of the three outcomes: total 1.71 (1.02 to 2.39) for unblinded or single-blind studies against 1.45 (1.15 to 1.75) for double-blind; positive 1.32 (0.96 to 1.67) against 1.68 (1.30 to 2.07); negative 0.98 (0.63 to 1.34) against 1.29 (1.09 to 1.50).

tasks.locator: Results > Total Psychopathological Symptoms, 1st paragraph, and Results > Positive Psychotic Symptoms, 1st paragraph (the lists of pooled studies); Table, BPRS Studies rows; Results > Effects of Ketamine in Patients With Schizophrenia, 1st paragraph
tasks.extracted: Overlap between the pooled figures and the single studies cited beside them: Newcomer et al. (1999) is reference 31 and stands in both the total-symptom and the positive-symptom lists, with 15 participants in the Table, so it sits inside the pooled estimates. Malhotra et al. (1997) is reference 25 and is pooled as well, with 16 healthy participants in the Table and 13 patients with schizophrenia in the narrative part; it is a companion report from the laboratory of Malhotra et al. (1996). Krystal et al. (1994) is not among the 36 pooled studies: it appears only as reference 5, in a meta-regression list.

tasks.locator: Abstract > Results, read against Results > Total Psychopathological Symptoms, Positive Psychotic Symptoms and Negative Symptoms, 2nd paragraphs
tasks.extracted: The abstract gives an I2 range of 77% to 83% for the inconsistency between studies, while the Results give I2 of 75.7% (total), 74.9% (positive) and 64.6% (negative); no value of 77% or 83% appears in the main text, and two of the three Results values fall in the review's own medium band (25% to 75%) rather than the high band the abstract's range implies. The heterogeneity figures this claim gives are the Results values.

tasks.locator: III. Pharmacodynamics of Ketamine and Its Metabolites, 2nd paragraph of the introductory section
tasks.extracted: Where the review introduces the metabolite account it names the evidence on both sides in one sentence: the two hydroxynorketamines are reported to produce antidepressant-relevant behaviour in rodents (its own authors' 2016 report and one independent study), followed by a parenthesis pointing to two independent studies that did not find this. The counter-evidence is named only there and its arguments are not described.
